extracted.intended_audience: Public housing agencies (PHAs), project owners, mortgagees, responsible entities, and applicants/tenants affected by HUD Section 214 noncitizen assistance restrictions
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements (definitions, documentary, verification, notice, appeal, hearing, and recordkeeping rules) implementing Section 214 of the Housing and Community Development Act governing eligibility for HUD financial assistance with respect to citizenship and immigration status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elderly family
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a family whose head (including co-head), spouse, or sole member is a person who is at least 62 years of age. It may include two or more persons who are at least 62 years of age living together, or one or more persons who are at least 62 years of age living with one or more live-in aides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes, but is not limited to, specified categories regardless of sexual orientation, gender identity, or marital status: (1) a single person (including elderly, displaced, disabled, near-elderly, otherwise eligible youth aged 18–24 who left foster care), or (2) a group of persons residing together including families with/without children, elderly families, near-elderly families, disabled families, displaced families, and remaining members of tenant families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live-in aide
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a person who resides with one or more elderly, near-elderly, or disabled persons and who: (1) is determined to be essential to the care and well‑being of the persons; (2) is not obligated for the support of the persons; and (3) would not be living in the unit except to provide the necessary supportive services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Near-elderly family
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a family whose head (including co-head), spouse, or sole member is at least 50 but under 62 years of age; or two or more persons at least 50 but under 62 living together; or one or more such persons living with one or more live-in aides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a person who (1)(i) has a disability as defined in 42 U.S.C. 423; (ii) is determined pursuant to HUD regulations to have a physical, mental, or emotional impairment that (A) is expected to be of long-continued and indefinite duration, (B) substantially impedes ability to live independently, and (C) could be improved by more suitable housing conditions; or (iii) has a developmental disability as defined in 42 U.S.C. 6001; (2) does not exclude persons with AIDS or conditions arising from its etiologic agent; (3) does not include persons whose disability is based solely on drug or alcohol dependence for low-income housing qualification; and (4) means “individual with handicaps” for reasonable accommodation and program accessibility purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability — Covered programs/assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart implements Section 214 and applies to financial assistance under specified programs: Section 235 Program, Section 236 Program (tenants paying below market rent only), Section 101 Rent Supplement Program, and the United States Housing Act of 1937 (HUD Public Housing, Section 8 Housing Assistance, Housing Development Grant Programs with respect to low income units).

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered individuals and entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions apply to both applicants for assistance and persons already receiving assistance (covered individuals/families), and to responsible entities defined as PHAs, project/housing owners, and mortgagees under the Section 235 Program (collectively 'responsible entity').

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide notices/documents in understood language
rubrics_metrics.description: For any notice or document this subpart requires the responsible entity to provide to an individual or to obtain the individual's signature on, the responsible entity, where feasible, must arrange for the notice/document to be provided in a language that is understood by the individual if the individual is not proficient in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 24 CFR 8.6 for communication with persons with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of citizenship or eligible status — general requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility for assistance or continued assistance under a Section 214 covered program is contingent upon a family's submission to the responsible entity of the documents described in § 5.508(b) for each family member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If family members do not have citizenship or eligible immigration status they may elect not to contend to have eligible status under paragraph (e) and preservation provisions (§§ 5.516 and 5.518) may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required for U.S. citizens or nationals
rubrics_metrics.description: For U.S. citizens or U.S. nationals, the evidence consists of a signed declaration of U.S. citizenship or nationality. The responsible entity may request verification by requiring presentation of a U.S. passport or other documentation as specified in HUD guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required for certain noncitizens (62+ on assistance Sept 30, 1996 or applying on/after that date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Noncitizens who are 62 years of age or older (or will be and receiving/ applying on/after Sept 30, 1996) must submit: (i) a signed declaration of eligible immigration status; and (ii) proof of age document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required for all other noncitizens
rubrics_metrics.description: All other noncitizens must submit: (i) a signed declaration of eligible immigration status, (ii) one of the INS documents referred to in § 5.510, and (iii) a signed verification consent form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each family member who contends he/she is a U.S. citizen or noncitizen with eligible immigration status must submit a written declaration signed under penalty of perjury indicating the status; adults sign for themselves, and an adult residing in unit and responsible for a child signs for the child. For Housing covered programs, the declaration may be part of the application or a separate document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification consent form — who signs and notice content
rubrics_metrics.description: Each noncitizen who declares eligible immigration status (except certain 62+ noncitizens) must sign a verification consent form: adults sign for themselves and an adult resident signs for children. The form must state that evidence of eligible status may be released without responsibility for further use to HUD and the INS for verification, and notify of possible release by HUD (only to INS for eligibility purposes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Individuals who elect not to contend to have eligible status
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more family members elect not to contend to have eligible immigration status, and other members establish citizenship/eligible status, the family may be eligible under §§ 5.516 and 5.518 or § 5.520; the family must identify in writing which members elect not to contend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of requirements of Section 214 — timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible entity must notify applicants at time of application; tenants at time of regular reexamination (but not later than one year following June 19, 1995); and mortgagors receiving Section 235 assistance must be provided notification and any additional Section 235 requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with pending applications on June 19, 1995 must be notified as soon as possible after that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of requirements of Section 214 — form and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice must (i) state that assistance is contingent upon submission and verification of evidence of citizenship/eligible status; (ii) describe the type of evidence and state the time period for submission; and (iii) state that assistance will be prorated, denied, or terminated upon final determination of ineligibility after appeals are exhausted (and inform tenants how to obtain preservation of families assistance under §§ 5.516 and 5.518).

rubrics_metrics.name: When evidence of eligible status is required to be submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible entity shall require evidence at specified times: (1) Applicants: not later than the date verification of other eligibility aspects will occur (§ 5.512(a)). (2) Tenants: at first regular reexamination after June 19, 1995 (except Section 235 payments). (3) New occupants: at first interim or regular reexamination following occupancy. (4) Changing participation: in accordance with subpart unless evidence already submitted. (5) One-time evidence requirement: each family member submits evidence only one time during continuously assisted occupancy under any Section 214 covered program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time to submit evidence — when must be granted
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsible entity must extend the time to submit evidence if the family member: (i) submits the declaration certifying the person is a noncitizen with eligible status; and (ii) certifies that evidence is temporarily unavailable, additional time is needed, and prompt and diligent efforts will be undertaken to obtain it. Any extension shall not exceed 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determination of extension length is based on individual circumstances; grant/denial must be in writing and explain reasons or specify period granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to submit evidence or to establish eligible status — consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If required evidence is not submitted within the time specified (including any extension), or if submitted evidence fails to establish eligible immigration status, the responsible entity shall proceed to deny, prorate or terminate assistance, or provide continued assistance or temporary deferral of termination, as appropriate, under §§ 5.514, 5.516, and 5.518.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents of eligible immigration status — originals and retention of copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible entity shall request and review original documents of eligible immigration status, retain photocopies for records, and return original documents to the family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable evidence is the original of a document designated by INS as acceptable in the six categories mentioned in § 5.506(a) for the specific status claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of eligible immigration status — primary and secondary
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary verification is conducted via INS automated SAVE system. If SAVE does not verify eligible status, secondary verification is a manual INS records search initiated by forwarding photocopies of original INS documents with form G-845S (or other INS-specified form) within 10 days of primary failure. If secondary verification does not confirm status, responsible entity must issue notice including right to appeal to INS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsible entity not liable for any action, delay, or failure of INS in conducting verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHA election to provide assistance before verification
rubrics_metrics.description: A PHA that is a responsible entity may elect to provide assistance to a family before verification of the eligibility of the individual or one family member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on delay, denial, reduction or termination of assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistance may not be delayed, denied, reduced or terminated on the basis of ineligible immigration status except as provided. Specifically, assistance shall not be delayed/denied/reduced/terminated if: (i) primary and secondary verification of timely-submitted documents not completed; (ii) family member lacking evidence has moved from unit; (iii) family member determined ineligible following INS verification has moved from unit; (iv) INS appeals process not concluded; (v) assistance is prorated in accordance with § 5.520; (vi) assistance for a mixed family is continued under §§ 5.516 and 5.518; or (vii) deferral of termination is granted under §§ 5.516 and 5.518. Additional restriction: for tenants, assistance cannot be delayed/denied/reduced/terminated until completion of the informal hearing described in paragraph (f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Events causing denial or termination of assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistance shall be denied for applicants and terminated for tenants upon occurrence of: (i) evidence/declaration not submitted by specified date or extension expiration; (ii) evidence timely submitted but INS primary/secondary verification does not verify eligible status and (A) family does not pursue INS appeal or informal hearing, or (B) appeals/hearing decided against family member; or (iii) responsible entity determines a family member knowingly permitted an ineligible individual to reside permanently in unit (termination period not less than 24 months; does not apply if ineligibility was considered in proration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See paragraph (i) for termination of assisted occupancy specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of denial or termination of assistance — required content
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice must advise the family: (1) that financial assistance will be denied/terminated with brief reason; (2) that family may be eligible for proration under § 5.520; (3) for tenants, criteria/procedures for preservation of families under §§ 5.514 and 5.518; (4) right to request INS appeal of secondary verification and to submit additional documentation; (5) right to request an informal hearing with responsible entity either upon completion of INS appeal or in lieu of INS appeal; (6) for applicants, that assistance may not be delayed until INS appeal concludes, but may be delayed during the informal hearing pendency; and other pertinent guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to the INS — procedures and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon notification that INS secondary verification failed, family has 30 days from the responsible entity's notification to request an appeal in writing directly to INS, provide the responsible entity with a copy and proof of mailing, and forward any additional documentation or written explanation (including form G-845S copy or other INS-specified form and cover letter). INS will issue a decision within 30 days of receipt; if delayed INS will notify family and responsible entity of reasons. Responsible entity must notify family of right to request an informal hearing upon receipt of INS decision. Pending INS appeal, assistance may not be delayed/denied/reduced/terminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal hearing procedures — rights and processes
rubrics_metrics.description: After INS decision or in lieu of INS appeal, family may request a hearing within 30 days of the responsible entity notice or INS decision. For families under Housing covered programs and applicants, informal hearing must provide: (A) hearing before an impartial individual (not the decisionmaker or subordinate), (B) opportunity to examine and copy documents in possession of responsible entity (or INS as permitted), (C) opportunity to present evidence and arguments in support of eligible status (evidence may be considered without regard to judicial evidentiary rules), (D) opportunity to controvert evidence relied upon by responsible entity and to confront/cross-examine witnesses, (E) right to be represented by attorney or designee at family's expense, (F) right to arrange for an interpreter (at family or responsible entity expense as agreed), and (G) right to have hearing recorded by audiotape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal hearing decision timeframe and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsible entity shall provide the family with a written final decision, based solely on the facts presented at the hearing, within 14 days of the date of the informal hearing. The decision shall state the basis for the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial relief
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision adverse to a family member under the INS appeal or informal hearing procedures does not preclude the family from seeking redress directly through judicial procedures if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of documents — 5 year requirement and list
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible entity shall retain for a minimum of 5 years documents submitted by the family or provided during INS appeal/informal hearing: (1) application for assistance; (2) income reexamination form; (3) photocopies of original documents (front/back), including INS documents; (4) signed verification consent form; (5) INS verification results; (6) request for INS appeal; (7) final INS determination; (8) request for informal hearing; and (9) final informal hearing decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of assisted occupancy — procedural options
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Housing covered programs and Section 8 programs other than Section 8 Rental Voucher and Moderate Rehabilitation, assisted occupancy is terminated by: (i) if permitted under lease, notifying tenant that tenant must pay HUD-approved market rent; (ii) entering into new lease without financial assistance; or (iii) eviction (responsible entity may continue assistance payments while eviction proceedings promptly initiated and diligently pursued in accordance with lease and applicable HUD and local law; HUD may prescribe maximum continuation period and standards of reasonable diligence). For Section 8 Rental Voucher and Moderate Rehabilitation programs, assisted occupancy is terminated by terminating assistance payments; PHA shall not make additional payments to owner after required procedures completed and shall not approve lease/assistance contract or process portability move after completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of preservation assistance to mixed families — types
rubrics_metrics.description: Preservation assistance is available to tenant mixed families following completion of appeals and informal hearing procedures. Three types: (i) Continued assistance (§ 5.518(a)), (ii) Temporary deferral of termination of assistance (§ 5.518(b)), and (iii) Prorated assistance (§ 5.520) (a mixed family must be provided prorated assistance if the family so requests). Availability depends on eligibility under the Housing covered programs.
